chunks: Hamza ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd ibn Ali ibn Al-Husayn ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) narrated in Qum in Rajab of the year 339 A.H. that Ali ibn Hashim informed me via a letter written in the year 307 A.H. that Yasir the servant narrated to him.

When Ar-Rida (peace be upon him) had a private session, he gathered all his servants, young and old, to be with him, talking to them and making them feel comfortable. When he sat at the table, he did not leave out anyone young or old, not even the horse caretaker or the phlebotomist, but seated them with him at his table.

Yasir said: One day while we were with him, we heard the sound of the lock on the door connecting Al-Ma'mun's house to the house of Abi Al-Hasan (peace be upon him). Ar-Rida (peace be upon him) said to us, 'Stand up and disperse.' We stood up. Al-Ma'mun came with a long letter. Ar-Rida intended to stand, but Al-Ma'mun swore by the right of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) that he should not stand up.

Then he came and leaned over Abi Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), kissed his face, and sat on a cushion in front of him, reading the letter to him. It was a report of the conquest of some towns of Kabul, stating: 'We have conquered such and such a town.'
When he finished, Ar-Rida (peace be upon him) asked him, 'Does the conquest of one of the towns of the polytheists make you happy?' Al-Ma'mun replied, 'Is there not joy in that?'

He said, 'O Commander of the Faithful! Fear God regarding the nation of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) and the authority God has given you and made special for you. You have neglected the affairs of the Muslims, delegating them to others who rule them with a ruling other than God's. You have stayed in this land and left the House of Emigration (Medina) and the place of revelation's descent. The Emigrants and Helpers are oppressed there, and no one respects the bond or covenant of a believer in their presence. A time comes for the oppressed where they exhaust themselves and cannot afford their expenses, finding no one to complain to and unable to reach you.'

'So fear God, O Commander of the Faithful, regarding the affairs of the Muslims, and return to the home of Prophethood and the source of the Emigrants and Helpers. Do you not know, O Commander of the Faithful, that the ruler of the Muslims is like the central pillar of a tent; whoever wants to attack the tent captures the pillar.'

Al-Ma'mun said, 'O my Master! What do you think?' He said, 'I think you should leave this land and move to the place of your fathers and forefathers, and look after the affairs of the Muslims, not leaving them to others, for God the Exalted will question you regarding what He gave you authority over.'

Al-Ma'mun stood up and said, 'Well said, O my Master! This is the opinion.' He went out and ordered the riding animals to be brought forward. This reached Thul-Riasatayn (the man of the two chiefdoms), who was deeply grieved, as he had dominated the affairs and Al-Ma'mun had no opinion of his own with him, so he did not dare to confront him.

Then Ar-Rida (peace be upon him) became very strong, and Thul-Riasatayn came to Al-Ma'mun and said, 'O Commander of the Faithful! What is this opinion you have ordered?' He said, 'My Master Abi Al-Hasan ordered me to do so, and it is correct.'

He said, 'O Commander of the Faithful! This is not correct. Yesterday you killed your brother and removed the Caliphate from him. Your father's children, all the people of Iraq, your family, and the Arabs are hostile to you. Then you introduced this second event: that you made Abi Al-Hasan the successor to the Caliphate and took it from your own children. The public, scholars, jurists, and the family of Abbas do not accept this, and their hearts are alienated from you.'

'The opinion is that you stay in Khorasan until people's hearts calm down with this and forget what happened to your brother Muhammad. And here, O Commander of the Faithful, there are elders who served Al-Rashid and knew the affair; consult them about this. If they advise it, then proceed.'

Al-Ma'mun said, 'Like those who said like Ali ibn Abi Imran, Ibn Munis, and Al-Jaludi?' Thul-Riasatayn said, 'Yes, these are the ones who resented the allegiance to Abi Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and did not accept it, so Al-Ma'mun imprisoned them for this reason.' Al-Ma'mun said, 'Yes.'

The next day, Abi Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) came and entered upon Al-Ma'mun, saying, 'O Commander of the Faithful! What have you done?' He recounted to him what Thul-Riasatayn had said. Al-Ma'mun summoned those men and brought them out of prison.

The first to enter was Ali ibn Abi Imran. He looked at Ar-Rida (peace be upon him) sitting beside Al-Ma'mun and said, 'I seek refuge in God, O Commander of the Faithful, that you take this affair which God has established for you and made special for you, and place it in the hands of your enemies, whose fathers you killed and scattered in the land.'
Al-Ma'mun said to him, 'O son of the fornicatress! And you are still upon this?' He said, 'Bring him forward, O Guard, and behead him.' So his neck was struck.
Then Ibn Munis was brought in. When he looked at Ar-Rida (peace be upon him) beside Al-Ma'mun, he said, 'O Commander of the Faithful! This one beside you, by God, is an idol worshipped besides God.'
Al-Ma'mun said to him, 'O son of the fornicatress! And you are still upon this?' He said, 'O Guard, bring him forward and behead him.' So he struck his neck.

Then Al-Jaludi was brought in. Al-Jaludi, during the Caliphate of Al-Rashid, when Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad revolted in Medina, Al-Rashid sent him and ordered him: if he captured him, to behead him, and to raid the houses of the family of Abi Talib, and to strip their women, leaving no one of them with more than one garment. Al-Jaludi did that.
After Abi Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) passed away, Al-Jaludi came to the door of Abi Al-Hasan Ar-Rida (peace be upon him) and besieged his house with his cavalry.

When Ar-Rida (peace be upon him) saw him, he gathered all the women in a room and stood at the door. Al-Jaludi said to Abi Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'I must enter the room and strip them, as the Commander of the Faithful has ordered me.'

Ar-Rida (peace be upon him) said, 'I will strip them for you, and I swear I will not leave anything on them that you do not take.' He kept asking him and swearing to him until he calmed down. Then Abi Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) entered.
He did not leave anything on them, not even their earrings, anklets, or girdles, but took it from them, along with all that was in the house, little or much.
On this day, when Al-Jaludi was brought to Al-Ma'mun, Ar-Rida (peace be upon him) said, 'O Commander of the Faithful! Grant me this old man.'
Al-Ma'mun said, 'O my Master! This is the one who did to the daughters of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) what he did by stripping them.'

Al-Jaludi looked at Ar-Rida (peace be upon him) as he was speaking to Al-Ma'mun, asking him to pardon him and grant him to him. He thought that he was helping against him because of what Al-Jaludi had done.
He said, 'O Commander of the Faithful! I ask you by God and by my service to Al-Rashid that you do not accept his word regarding me.'

Al-Ma'mun said, 'O Abi Al-Hasan! He has asked for pardon, and we fulfill his oath.' Then he said, 'No, by God, I will not accept his word regarding you. Attach him to his two companions.' He was brought forward and his neck was struck.

Thul-Riasatayn returned to his father Sahl. Al-Ma'mun had ordered the riding animals to be brought forward, but Thul-Riasatayn had refused. When Al-Ma'mun killed these men, Thul-Riasatayn knew that he had resolved to leave.

Ar-Rida (peace be upon him) said, 'O Commander of the Faithful! What did you do regarding the bringing forward of the riding animals?' Al-Ma'mun said, 'O my Master! You order them to do so.' Abi Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) went out and called to the people, 'Bring forward the riding animals!'
It was as if fire had fallen upon them. The riding animals came forward and went out. Thul-Riasatayn remained in his house.

Al-Ma'mun sent for him, and he came. He said to him, 'What is wrong with you? Why did you sit in your house?' He said, 'O Commander of the Faithful! My sin is great in the sight of your family and the public. People blame me for killing your deposed brother and for the allegiance to Ar-Rida (peace be upon him). I do not fear the whisperers, the envious, and the rebels from conspiring against me. So let me stay behind in Khorasan.'
Al-Ma'mun said to him, 'We do not dispense with you.' As for what you said about the conspiracies and enmity, you are the trusted one with us, the faithful, cautious Al-Ma'mun.

'Write for yourself whatever guarantee and security you trust in, and confirm for yourself whatever makes you feel secure.' He went and wrote a letter for himself, gathered scholars on it, and brought it to Al-Ma'mun.

He read it, and Al-Ma'mun gave him whatever he liked, and wrote for him in his own handwriting the letter of grant: 'I have granted you such and such from wealth, property, and authority,' and expanded his worldly hopes for him.

Thul-Riasatayn said, 'O Commander of the Faithful! It is necessary that the handwriting of Abi Al-Hasan be in this letter of security, granting us what you granted, for he is the successor to your covenant.'

Al-Ma'mun said, 'You know that Abi Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) has stipulated with us that he will not do anything from that and will not introduce a new event, so we do not ask him what he dislikes. Ask him yourself, for he will not refuse you in this.'

He came and asked permission to enter upon Abi Al-Hasan (peace be upon him). Yasir said: Ar-Rida (peace be upon him) said to us, 'Stand up and move aside.' We moved aside. He entered and stood before him for a while.

Abi Al-Hasan raised his head to him and said, 'What is your need, O Fadl?' He said, 'O my Master! This is what the Commander of the Faithful wrote for me. You are more worthy to give us what the Commander of the Faithful gave, since you are the successor to the covenant of the Muslims.'

Ar-Rida (peace be upon him) said to him, 'Read it.' It was a letter on large leather. He remained standing until he read it. When he finished, Abi Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said to him, 'O Fadl! For you with us is this, as long as you fear God the Exalted.'
Yasir said: He nullified his affair for him in a single word. He left from him, Al-Ma'mun left, and we left with Ar-Rida (peace be upon him).

After a few days, while we were at one of the waystations, a letter came to Thul-Riasatayn from his brother Al-Hasan ibn Sahl: 'I looked into the calculation of the stars regarding the transition of this year and found that you will taste the heat of iron and fire on Wednesday of such and such a month.'

'I think that you, Ar-Rida, and the Commander of the Faithful should enter the bathhouse on this day, and you should undergo cupping there, pouring the blood on your body so that the bad omen is removed from you.'
So Al-Fadl sent to Al-Ma'mun and wrote to him about this, asking him to enter the bathhouse with him and to ask Abi Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about this as well.
Al-Ma'mun wrote to Ar-Rida (peace be upon him) a note about this and asked him. Abi Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) wrote back to him, 'I will not enter the bathhouse tomorrow.'
'And I do not see it wise for you, O Commander of the Faithful, to enter the bathhouse tomorrow, nor for Al-Fadl to enter the bathhouse tomorrow.' He sent the note back to him twice.

Abi Al-Hasan wrote back, 'I will not enter the bathhouse tomorrow, for I saw the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) in my sleep last night saying to me, 'O Ali! Do not enter the bathhouse tomorrow.'

'So I do not see it wise for you, O Commander of the Faithful, nor for Al-Fadl to enter the bathhouse tomorrow.' Al-Ma'mun wrote back, 'You are right, O my Master, and the Messenger of Allah is right. I will not enter the bathhouse tomorrow, and Al-Fadl [will do as he knows].'
Yasir said: When we had evening and the sun set, Ar-Rida (peace be upon him) said to us, 'Say: I seek refuge in God from the evil of what will descend tonight.' We began saying that.
When Ar-Rida (peace be upon him) prayed Fajr, he said to us, 'Say: I seek refuge in God from the evil of what will descend today.' We continued saying that.
When it was near sunrise, Ar-Rida (peace be upon him) said, 'Go up to the roof and listen, do you hear anything?' When I went up, I heard the clamor and wailing, and it increased.
Al-Ma'mun entered from the door that was to his house from the house of Abi Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), saying, 'O my Master! O Abi Al-Hasan! May God reward you for Al-Fadl.'

He had entered the bathhouse, and some men came to him with swords and killed him. Those who entered with him in the bathhouse were taken, and they were three men, one of whom was Al-Fadl's maternal cousin, Thul-Qalamayn.
The commanders and soldiers, and those who were from the men of Thul-Riasatayn, gathered at the door of Al-Ma'mun, saying, 'He tricked him and killed him, so we will surely seek blood for him.'
Al-Ma'mun said to Ar-Rida (peace be upon him), 'O my Master! Do you think of going out to them and dispersing them?'

Yasir said: Ar-Rida (peace be upon him) mounted and said to me, 'Mount.' When we went out of the door, Ar-Rida (peace be upon him) looked at them, and they had gathered and brought fire to burn the door.
He called out to them and gestured to them with his hand, 'Disperse!' So they dispersed.
Yasir said: The people came forward, by God, some falling over others. He did not gesture to anyone except that he ran past, and no one stopped him.

key_terms.الرِّضَا: Ar-Rida (the Acceptance), a title for Imam Ali ibn Musa (a.s.)
key_terms.الْجَلُودِيُّ: Al-Jaludi, a military commander known for looting the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.ذُو الرِّئَاسَتَيْنِ: Thul-Riasatayn (The Man of the Two Chiefdoms), referring to Fadl ibn Sahl

ai.seo_question: What happened between Imam Ar-Rida (a.s.) and Al-Ma'mun regarding the succession and the death of Al-Fadl?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Yun al-Akhbar* illustrates the political tension between Imam Ar-Rida (a.s.) and Caliph Al-Ma'mun, highlighting the Imam’s strategic acceptance of succession to preserve the lineage of prophethood while critiquing the Abbasid deviation from Islamic governance. The narrative underscores the theme of *ghaybah* (occultation) precursors and the Imam’s spiritual authority over temporal power, as seen when his advice leads to the assassination of Fadl ibn Sahl and his subsequent dispersal of the troops through divine presence. It serves as a key text in Shia scholarship for understanding the dynamics of *taqiyyah* and the Imam’s role as the true guide amidst political turmoil.
